text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's German newspapers:
- Parliamentary leader of CDU, Wolfgang Schaeuble, reaffirms his readiness to compromise on tax reform proposals with opposition SPD.

- Former East German leader Egon Krenz, on trial and charged with manslaughter for responsibility for deaths at the Berlin Wall, said he was not responsible. The 18-month-long trial concludes on Monday when verdict expected.
- European shareholders hold their nerves. DAX index falls 1.8 percent. Experts urge buying at low levels.
- IG Metall union urges cuts in working hours as union fights for five percent more pay for 8,000 workers in eastern German steel industry.
- Steep slide in share prices stopped. No panic selling on world bourses, share prices recover, DAX holds above 4,000 points. No 'black Monday' thanks to calm reaction of shareholders.
- Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt says exports boosting German economy. Rexrodt demands tax cuts. Economy waiting for signals from political leaders on tax reform.

- Holocaust survivors suing Allianz and German insurers for billions. Lawyers representing victims sue 16 European firms for a total of $16 billion for life insurance policies not paid out to survivors.
- Volkswagen profits rise sharply. Profits rise 73 percent in the first half to 488 million marks. Sales rise 12 percent to 56 billion marks. Company cities stronger dollar and cost cutting measures.
- Share prices fall on almost all bourses. Decline not as steep as expected. No panic selling. DAX falls only briefly below 4,000 point level. Experts urge shareholders to wait.
- Rexrodt says there will be fewer unemployed in 1998.
- No 'black Monday'. German share prices down 1.79 percent. Dollar weakens. Small shareholders react calmly.
- Rexrodt expects upturn on jobs market.
